summary: A satirical news-style feature on how mainstream fashion has been borrowing from underground, 'subterranean' style since late 2023. It traces key moments, designers and boutiques, and the tension between influence and appropriation as once-exclusive looks are commodified. It concludes that the underground keeps moving on to newer styles as the mainstream catches up.
one_line: A satirical feature on mainstream fashion's commodification of subterranean style from late 2023 into 2024, and the underground's constant move to something new.
key_facts: Allegra Martinez wore a patched-up denim jacket over a holographic catsuit at her gallery opening in Lower East Side Manhattan on October 4, 2023.
Photos of Allegra Martinez's look were on fashion mood boards from New York to New Delhi by midnight.
Lovisa Engberg is a Swedish designer who started by sewing her dockworker dad's tar-soiled jeans into corset-like contraptions.
Lovisa Engberg's brand is called "Gruvan", and the note says it means something very deep in Swedish.
Engberg's "Sub-Metro" collection reached mainstream awareness on November 8, 2023, featuring heelless work boots and upcycled biker jackets with removable, interchangeable sleeves.
In mid-November 2023, Blade, a single-named street-style icon turned retail mogul, opened the boutique "Below" on Rodeo Drive.
Activists in the subterranean sphere argue that Blade's boutique is a hostile takeover of their threads and cred, though Blade calls it homage.
Quentin Rafferty, an underground blogger and fashion critic, said "The irony is malnourishing" and criticized $300 pre-torn jeans.
Petar Petrović showed his "Neo-Industri" line on a dirt runway in the catacombs of Berlin on December 2, 2023, including repurposed safety goggles as eyewear.
Rumors suggest Petrović's goggles will be worn by Silicon Valley techies by Spring 2024.
By mid-December 2023, teens at malls wore utility belts over mesh shirts and bucket hats.
Tiffany Huang, a Gen Z consultant on cultural capital, described a "cycle of continuous excavation" in which exclusive styles are unearthed for mass consumption.
By January 2024, the fashion world had declared subterranean couture the must-have look of the season, though its half-life was already decaying.
